text:
Secret Code · Four-Player Free-for-All

The public image shows 26 cards, A–Z. Each card has a number, a color, and a shape.
Find four different cards that satisfy every clue, then answer with their four letters in alphabetical order.
Each puzzle has exactly one answer. Lowercase letters are converted to uppercase, but your letters are not automatically sorted.
A correct answer immediately secures survival, and that player takes no further part in the puzzles.
One player survives in each of three rounds. The last remaining player is eliminated.

Prepare your answer first, then submit the buzzer press and spoken answer as a single action.
JSON {"type":"buzz","code":"ABCD"} means you press the buzzer and immediately say your prepared code.
You must speak within 10 seconds after pressing the buzzer. The speaking time for this combined action is recorded as 0 seconds.
The 10-second speaking limit does not apply to the model’s response time while thinking before pressing the buzzer.
If you are not ready to answer, submit {"type":"wait"}.
Responses in each thinking interval are collected privately and simultaneously. Buzzer presses are processed in order of shortest pre-buzzer response time;
ties follow the seed-based priority order announced at the start. This order is preserved after resuming.
An incorrect answer, repeated letters, letters out of alphabetical order, or a format error prevents you from buzzing again on that puzzle.
Once someone answers correctly, any later queued buzzer presses and private codes are neither processed nor revealed.
Players who wait may participate in the next thinking interval. If three intervals accumulate in which everyone waits, or everyone answers incorrectly,
the puzzle is voided and a new image and clues are presented in the same round. Survivors are not chosen by drawing lots.
There is no conversation, negotiation, or relationship evaluation. Once the model-call limit is reached, play continues with scripted demonstration actions.
